name: securing-clip-hero
prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: 16:9 wide premium landing page hero and cinematic product reel still.
Primary request: Transform the reference CAD product into meticulous photoreal macro product photography, preserving its precise industrial design. Image 1 defines the installed assembly and visible longitudinal hinge; Image 2 verifies the exact elbow shell and two-tab clamp geometry and round barrel connector.
Scene: A dark laptop on a graphite desk, against a deep charcoal to near-black studio background. Place the product and the laptop's side edge in the center-right of a wide 16:9 composition, leaving the left 40% spacious near-black negative space. Close low three-quarter macro view with the entire gold elbow product readable, and just enough dark laptop keyboard and edge to explain attachment.
Subject invariants: Same compact gold-colored 90-degree tubular elbow clamshell surrounding a black round laptop power cable. The long cylindrical gold arm meets the shorter cylindrical gold arm at exactly a rounded right-angle elbow, not a rectangular box or generic cable holder. Preserve the thin silver longitudinal piano hinge along the long arm. At the laptop-side end is the original gray two-tab edge clamp, one tab above and one below the laptop edge, and one small vertical silver screw in the upper tab. Cable exits the original opposite end and routes away. Gray ribbed liner remains internal and hidden in this closed-shell installed shot. The power connection is a round barrel connection concealed in the installation.
Materials: finely textured satin champagne gold shell with restrained real metal reflections, gray machined clamp, black polymer cable, dark anodized laptop. Elegant warm rim light tracing the gold elbow, soft cool fill, subtle realistic desk shadow, shallow but sufficient depth of field for product geometry, crisp beautiful detail.
Constraints: Preserve the reference engineering and scale; change only photographic finish, lighting, background, camera composition, and dark laptop styling. No redesigned connectors, no USB-C, no generic desk clip, no extraneous screw, no labels, no logos, no overlay text, no watermark.

name: securing-clip-beauty
prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: 16:9 wide premium product beauty photograph for a cinematic reel and landing page.
Primary request: Re-render the exact reference product as extraordinarily realistic, refined studio product photography. Preserve the CAD reference's recognizable industrial geometry precisely.
Scene/backdrop: seamless dark charcoal satin studio surface and background with a soft grounded shadow under the product; the product appears just slightly suspended above the surface. Clean uncluttered cinematic composition.
Subject: the entire original 90-degree gold tubular elbow clamshell, centered and fully visible in a wide 16:9 landscape frame. Preserve the same viewpoint as reference: black round power cable exits the left-facing tube opening and travels to the lower-left edge; gold cylindrical tube bends smoothly at 90 degrees, with the second arm running to the right. At its right end, the same small gray two-tab laptop-edge clamp surrounds the black connector base; a small silver vertical screw sits in the upper tab. A silver cylindrical round barrel power plug protrudes to the right and has the original dark circular center opening. No laptop in this detached beauty shot. A subtle longitudinal clamshell seam/hinge follows original geometry.
Materials/textures: finely textured satin champagne gold metal, restrained warm specular highlights, gray metal clamp, black polymer power cable, precise silver barrel connector. Large soft key light and elegant amber rim, lifelike reflections and microtexture. Tack-sharp core product with subtle photographic depth of field and luxurious contrast.
Constraints: Exact same elbow shape and clamp proportions as supplied. Keep both gray clamp tabs, one upper and one lower, the single small screw, and the cylindrical round barrel connector. Gray ribbed cable liner is hidden within closed shell. No redesign, no USB-C, no rectangular connector, no generic desk clip, no other objects, no typography, no logos, no watermark.

name: securing-clip-mechanism
prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: 16:9 wide macro mechanism beauty shot for a cinematic product reel and landing page.
Primary request: Turn Image 1's exact open-clamshell securing clip assembly into photoreal studio macro photography. Image 1 defines the exact open mechanism, all component positions and ribbed liner; Image 2 defines the same product's closed elbow and circular barrel connector. This is the same engineering, with a premium photography finish.
Scene/backdrop: open assembly centered over a matte charcoal studio surface, subtle grounded shadows, generous dark space around it, 16:9 landscape.
Composition/framing: faithfully preserve Image 1's overhead three-quarter layout. The gold tubular 90-degree elbow enclosure is split longitudinally on its original thin silver hinge and opened like a clamshell. The back half cradles the black cable and gray liner, the matching L-shaped front half folds open toward lower right. Preserve the actual elbow geometry, not a flat panel. A gray cylindrical ribbed sleeve with the same row of evenly spaced open transverse ribs wraps the straight section of black cable; the black cable makes its original right-angle bend at the rear and leaves toward upper left. The same original gray two-tab clamp protrudes at the left-facing connector end. The single small vertical silver clamp screw is detached and resting just in front of the open shell, as in Image 1. Preserve all visible assembly relationships, component count, and scale.
Materials/lighting: finely textured satin champagne gold outer shell with smooth warm metallic inner surface, gray ribbed liner and clamp with realistic subtle polymer texture, black cable, silver hinge and small screw. Precise soft studio light, warm grazing rim highlights, believable macro shadows, crisp focus revealing the liner and hinge.
Constraints: This is an open-clamshell mechanism view based exactly on reference, not an invented exploded diagram. Do not separate the liner from the cable or add floating parts. Preserve gray rib count and two clamp tabs as closely as possible. Use a round barrel power connector if visible, never USB-C. No generic desk clip, no redesign, no laptop, no callouts, no text, no logos, no watermark.
